candidates.evidence_text: A disabled mum from Greater Manchester has joined a campaign for better paternity leave after being "stopped in her tracks" by the challenges of adapting to motherhood alone Melissa Johns, 36, from Ashton-under-Lyne, welcomed her first child in October Despite requiring six weeks to recover from a caesarean section, Melissa - who was born without a fully formed right arm - was left to face maternity leave alone after her partner went back to work when their daughter was two weeks old She has now joined a campaign to change the law to let fathers take longer paternity leave, and to receive a bigger proportion of their salary when they do But sceptics say such changes would have a significant impact on businesses, and question how they could be afforded Melissa said: "Having one arm means that I rely on my core strength a lot more," Melissa said

candidates.evidence_text: A disabled mum from Greater Manchester has joined a campaign for better paternity leave after being "stopped in her tracks" by the challenges of adapting to motherhood alone Melissa Johns, 36, from Ashton-under-Lyne, welcomed her first child in October Despite requiring six weeks to recover from a caesarean section, Melissa - who was born without a fully formed right arm - was left to face maternity leave alone after her partner went back to work when their daughter was two weeks old She has now joined a campaign to change the law to let fathers take longer paternity leave, and to receive a bigger proportion of their salary when they do But sceptics say such changes would have a significant impact on businesses, and question how they could be afforded Melissa said: "Having one arm means that I rely on my core strength a lot more," Melissa said

candidates.evidence_text: Former boxing world champion Frank Bruno has distributed free footballs to local parks in support of a scheme encouraging children to get active The 64-year-old delivered 10 footballs to Southchurch Park in Southend-on-Sea and the nearby village of Hockley in Essex Ritchie Beckett, the director of non-profit initiative Found Football, is pledging to drop more of them in the county's parks before the end of the year The 44-year-old dad from Stockport said Bruno's support took the movement "to another level" and he wanted it to go "nationwide" in the future On social media, Bruno said he hoped it would prevent children from getting involved with "other activities" "If a small game of football between a few people means they won't be up to other things in the park it gets my thumbs up," said the former WBC heavyweight champion

candidates.evidence_text: Trade union members at the University of Greater Manchester have staged a protest demanding "greater transparency" following the sacking of the former vice chancellor professor George Holmes Unison members at the institution in Bolton said the current board of governors should step aside, arguing the university can only move on with a "clean slate" Holmes was suspended after the university commissioned an independent inquiry into allegations of financial mismanagement and other misconduct A university spokesperson said it "took the time to talk to staff members and listen to concerns raised" at the protest Unison representative Paul Chanin, said: "The current board of governors, who were around when George Holmes was around, need to look at themselves, to understand whether they should be remaining in post." Holmes had been in post for 20 years before he was suspended following an independent inquiry into allegations raised in an investigation by The Mill , external in 2025

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City's lease at the Etihad Stadium was placed under review last month amid a major expansion of the club's east Manchester campus, it has emerged City has a long-term lease at the ground with Manchester City Council and finished expanding its north stand earlier this year, which increased the stadium capacity to more than 60,000 people It has been building a new £300m entertainment zone known as Medlock Square which includes a Radisson Blu Hotel and a zip-line, with plans for a new 600-person capacity entertainment venue which the council granted planning permission in June The lease review was sparked as a result of changes taking place around the Etihad Campus, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) understands Council papers describing a decision about a "variation of leases with Manchester City Football Club" have been made public on the town hall's website but specifics of the finances have been kept hidden from view The review is expected to result in an uplift in the yearly base rate fee paid to the city council from the club, currently said to be between £3m to £4m a year

candidates.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council bin boss hits back at critics who say it's 'an absolute joke' Councillor Jake Austin said they were delivering what people want by increasing collections, a move welcomed by critics in the council Comments News Edward Barne Stockport council’s bin boss has hit back at critics after one councillor said the local authority’s response was ‘an absolute joke’. Councillor Jake Austin said they were delivering what people want by increasing collections Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved and last week, the council’s Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year. From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025. Opposition parties have overwhelmingly welcomed the move but questions remain

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Police watchdog gives update on synagogue terror attack investigations Terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie was shot dead by GMP firearms officers Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 17:45, 04 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Heaton Park Hebrew An investigation by the police watchdog into previous contact between Greater Manchester Police and terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie before the Manchester synagogue atrocity is expected to be finalised next year The Independent Office for Police Conduct said its probe was looking at 'the actions taken by police in response to reports of crimes committed by him'. Two separate IOPC investigations arising from the Yom Kippur attack on October 2 last year at Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation i Congregant Adrian Daulby, 53, died from 'a single gunshot wound to the chest' after police opened fire on Al-Shamie. He was helping to barricade the door of the synagogue as Al-Shamie was trying to get inside at the time. A coroner's court heard in October last year that 'a singl Melvin Cravitz, 66, died from 'multiple stab wounds' at Al-Shamie's hands. Mr Cravitz was earlier almost hit by the car the terrorist was driving. Al-Shamie went on to be shot dead by GMP firearms officers The IOPC launched two separate investigations - codenamed Keasden and Sandtoft - in the aftermath

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at the trial of 12 men accused of sexual offences after a husband allegedly drugged and raped his wife over a number of years The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges, including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent, rape and sexual assault. The charges relate to a 20 year period The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect the anonymity of his alleged victim. The law entitles the alleged victim to anonymity for life The other 12 defendants deny the charges against them. They are Karl Lindsay, Daniel Rayner, Graham Brougham, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir, Jonathan Kirk, Sean Peers, Jordan Wallace, Alan Keelan, Richard Townsend, Robert Stewart and David Graves. All charges relate to the same sin A jury of 12 people, nine women and three men, were sworn in at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (September 4). They were sent away until Wednesday morning (September 9). Two alternative jurors, two women, were also selected

candidates.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

Officers were called out to Alexandra Road, in Whalley Range , at around 1am this morning (September 4) Greater Manchester Police says a 25-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of drink driving. Officers went on to conduct a search, before seizing quantities of suspected Class A, B and C drugs The driver and his passenger, a 17-year-old boy, were subsequently arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply controlled drugs. The stationary vehicle was unoccupied at the time of the crash and no injuries were reported, GMP says Both suspects remain in custody for questioning this morning (Friday). The investigation remains ongoing, GMP says Images from the scene showed multiple GMP vehicles in attendance following the crash. An ambulance and two fire engines were also sent out to the scene

candidates.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.
candidates.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, Comments News David Dubas-Fisher Data Investigations Editor and Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 07:13, 05 Sep 2026 On a mild Friday afternoon, a handful of people are milling about the precinct in Brinnington, a suburb of Stockport nestled beside the M60 Just under six miles away, parking spaces are hard to come by in the leafy village of Bramhall . The difference is clear - one an area where people feel left behind, the other a place people aspire to call home The lives of Stopfordians in Brinnington and Bramhall are very different. They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, life expectancy According to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), men in Brinnington have an average healthy life expectancy of 50.5 years. That's the lowest in the Greater Manchester For men in Bramhall West, it's 75.3 years. That's the highest in Greater Manchester and one one of the highest in the country

candidates.evidence_text: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 05 Sep 2026 It was a link forged with blood sweat and tears. It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. Workers came from Ireland - around 5,000 of them. The others came from Scotland, Wales, and South West England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Manchester Evening News were circulated on a social media platform, understood to be TikTok, on Thursday evening (September 3). One showed a hand holding a bladed weapon while another showed an image of armed police The picture of the knife carried the caption: 'Coop Walkden I'm After You Next.' After officers were called in over the disturbing content on the social media site, the MEN was contacted by a number of concerned parents of children at Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford The school acted quickly with security being stepped up including increased monitoring of access. Bag checks were also carried out, with nothing untoward being found following the purported threats, which are being treated as a hoax A second image shared on the social media platform featured a picture of an armed police officer and the words 'them tomorrow at coop academy walkden.'

It's a scene of joy to watch the young and old play together View 6 Images The award-winning Fernlea Care Home, which has a children’s nursery, Fernbee’s on site (Image: Manchester Evening News) This is a care home with a difference. It’s home to residents, currently up to 106 years of age. But also on the site is the Fernbees nursery, with youngsters aged from just six months, who regularly pop in for a tea break or lunch The two communities happily mix in an inter-generational model that has won praise from both its care users and the wider industry. Our Lifestyle Editor Dianne Bourne popped down for a visit and brought us this joyful despatch After the sing song in the main lounge, Dianne watched as the kids and older residents moved over to the bar area to tuck in to some tea, squash and cakes and have a chit chat. She describes the lovely image of June - a former Stockport mayor - playing games with the younger kids “The kids behave beautifully, they really do. I did wonder at first but they’re just lovely."

candidates.lead: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event.
candidates.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event. “I hope one day - and I don't know whether it will be in my lifetime or not - there won't be a need for Pride because everyone will be equal,” says Steph Kay. “We're certainly not there yet.” It started with a few trestle tables and some games to raise money for AIDS sufferers. It transformed into a behemoth with international stars to rival the world’s biggest festivals View 4 Images All the thrills of the Manchester Gay Pub and Club Olympics in 1985 As a long-standing Gay Village businesswoman, Steph has seen Manchester Pride take many forms. The former manager of lesbian bar Vanilla has worked and partied throughout the event over decades. She was, at one time, a trustee of the event But Steph says the festival ‘snowballed’ after she left, with organisers deciding to hire bigger artists and venues. It was these decisions that culminated in the controversial choice to move Pride out of the Village entirely

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at the trial of 12 men accused of sexual offences after a husband allegedly drugged and raped his wife over a number of years The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges, including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent, rape and sexual assault. The charges relate to a 20 year period The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect the anonymity of his alleged victim. They are Karl Lindsay, Daniel Rayner, Graham Brougham, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir, Jonathan Kirk, Sean Peers, Jordan Wallace, Alan Keelan, Richard Townsend, Robert Stewart and David Graves. All charges relate to the same sin A jury of 12 people, nine women and three men, were sworn in at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (September 4). They were sent away until Wednesday morning (September 9). Two alternative jurors, two women, were also selected

candidates.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

candidates.evidence_text: Whalley Range Police descend on Whalley Range street at 1am with two arrested after driver smashes into parked car Officers seized drugs from the scene in Whalley Range, Manchester News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:18, 04 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Two people have been arrested after a driver ploughed into a parked car in south Manchester. Officers were called out to Alexandra Road, in Whalley Range , at around 1am this morning (September 4) Greater Manchester Police says a 25-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of drink driving. Officers went on to conduct a search, before seizing quantities of suspected Class A, B and C drugs The driver and his passenger, a 17-year-old boy, were subsequently arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply controlled drugs. The stationary vehicle was unoccupied at the time of the crash and no injuries were reported, GMP says Both suspects remain in custody for questioning this morning (Friday). The investigation remains ongoing, GMP says Images from the scene showed multiple GMP vehicles in attendance following the crash. An ambulance and two fire engines were also sent out to the scene

Emergency services attended Chorley New Road, in Horwich , at 10.37am on Thursday morning (September 3) Greater Manchester Police says officer responded to reports of a crash involving an MG HS Trophy. The vehicle was reportedly travelling at relatively low speed before it steered off the road and hit a bus stop It is believed the driver suffered a serious medical episode in the moments leading up to the collision. GMP says the driver suffered serious injuries No other people were involved, GMP says. The road was closed for a time following the collision, near to Chorley New Road Primary School. Enquiries are ongoing and witnesses are being urged to come forward A GMP spokesperson said: "As part of the investigation, our Serious Collision Investigation Unit are asking anyone with information to please come forward. Councillor Jake Austin said they were delivering what people want by increasing collections Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved and last week, the council’s Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year. From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, Comments News David Dubas-Fisher Data Investigations Editor and Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 07:13, 05 Sep 2026 On a mild Friday afternoon, a handful of people are milling about the precinct in Brinnington, a suburb of Stockport nestled beside the M60 Just under six miles away, parking spaces are hard to come by in the leafy village of Bramhall . The difference is clear - one an area where people feel left behind, the other a place people aspire to call home The lives of Stopfordians in Brinnington and Bramhall are very different. They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, life expectancy According to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), men in Brinnington have an average healthy life expectancy of 50.5 years. That's the lowest in the Greater Manchester For men in Bramhall West, it's 75.3 years. That's the highest in Greater Manchester and one one of the highest in the country

It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. Workers came from Ireland - around 5,000 of them. The others came from Scotland, Wales, and South West England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Manchester Evening News were circulated on a social media platform, understood to be TikTok, on Thursday evening (September 3). One showed a hand holding a bladed weapon while another showed an image of armed police The picture of the knife carried the caption: 'Coop Walkden I'm After You Next.' After officers were called in over the disturbing content on the social media site, the MEN was contacted by a number of concerned parents of children at Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford The school acted quickly with security being stepped up including increased monitoring of access. Bag checks were also carried out, with nothing untoward being found following the purported threats, which are being treated as a hoax A second image shared on the social media platform featured a picture of an armed police officer and the words 'them tomorrow at coop academy walkden.'

evidence_packet.summary: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Mancheste
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Manchester Evening News were circulated on a social media platform, understood to be TikTok, on Thursday evening (September 3). One showed a hand holding a bladed weapon while another showed an image of armed police The picture of the knife carried the caption: 'Coop Walkden I'm After You Next.' After officers were called in over the disturbing content on the social media site, the MEN was contacted by a number of concerned parents of children at Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford The school acted quickly with security being stepped up including increased monitoring of access. Bag checks were also carried out, with nothing untoward being found following the purported threats, which are being treated as a hoax A second image shared on the social media platform featured a picture of an armed police officer and the words 'them tomorrow at coop academy walkden.'

Councillor Jake Austin said they were delivering what people want by increasing collections Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved and last week, the council’s Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year. From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025. candidates.evidence_text: Three-year-old Nico wanders over to 96-year-old June with a bag filled with toys, and she rummages around to produce a rubber duckie to his beaming delight and squeals from the other kids. It's a scene of joy to watch the young and old play together View 6 Images The award-winning Fernlea Care Home, which has a children’s nursery, Fernbee’s on site (Image: Manchester Evening News) This is a care home with a difference. It’s home to residents, currently up to 106 years of age. But also on the site is the Fernbees nursery, with youngsters aged from just six months, who regularly pop in for a tea break or lunch The two communities happily mix in an inter-generational model that has won praise from both its care users and the wider industry. Our Lifestyle Editor Dianne Bourne popped down for a visit and brought us this joyful despatch After the sing song in the main lounge, Dianne watched as the kids and older residents moved over to the bar area to tuck in to some tea, squash and cakes and have a chit chat. She describes the lovely image of June - a former Stockport mayor - playing games with the younger kids “The kids behave beautifully, they really do. I did wonder at first but they’re just lovely."

candidates.lead: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event.
candidates.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event. “I hope one day - and I don't know whether it will be in my lifetime or not - there won't be a need for Pride because everyone will be equal,” says Steph Kay. “We're certainly not there yet.” It started with a few trestle tables and some games to raise money for AIDS sufferers. It transformed into a behemoth with international stars to rival the world’s biggest festivals View 4 Images All the thrills of the Manchester Gay Pub and Club Olympics in 1985 As a long-standing Gay Village businesswoman, Steph has seen Manchester Pride take many forms. The former manager of lesbian bar Vanilla has worked and partied throughout the event over decades. She was, at one time, a trustee of the event But Steph says the festival ‘snowballed’ after she left, with organisers deciding to hire bigger artists and venues. It was these decisions that culminated in the controversial choice to move Pride out of the Village entirely

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

candidates.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

candidates.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital Lancashire dad determined to walk daughter down the aisle hails Manchester trial as 'better than a lottery win' Jason Walker is fighting on thanks to a new trial at The Christie Comments News Amy Walters and Stephen Topping Senio A dad with incurable cancer is fighting on to walk his daughter down the aisle - and hopes to 'be around for at least 'another 10 years'. Jason Walker was given a devastating diagnosis after experiencing persistent back pain and double vision At first, he thought they were simply signs of ageing, but the symptoms only worsened. Jason was diagnosed with stage three multiple myeloma, a type of blood cancer, which was terminal He went on to spend five years in remission but last November several lumps were found, with tests confirming he had relapsed. But after becoming the first patient to take part in a new trial at The Christie , the 57-year-old has big plans for the future “I need to get through this, as I’m giving her away,” the painting business owner, from Lancashire , said. “I want to be well enough to walk my beautiful daughter down the aisle “It’s every father’s dream to give their little girl away. And for her to be happy and settled with the man she loves. I can’t wait for that moment to see her in her wedding dress - it will be emotional

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

candidates.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

The application detailed 30 reported shoplifting incidents from December 2025, resulting in losses of £3,994 to local businesses Lucas was brought to the attention of the Community Safety Service after retailers reported him for shoplifting up to three incidents a day. In each offence, he stole chocolate and confectionery Under the terms of the order, Lucas is banned from entering One Stop Community Shop and Tesco Express on Butler Green and Drury Convenience Store on Drury Lane, Chadderton

candidates.evidence_text: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale, which has lain empty for decades, has been transformed into a café, which will formally open this weekend Nestled in the heart of Denehurst Park, the café will occupy the ground floor of Denehurst House and visitors can see it for themselves when it formally opens its doors this Saturday (5 September) More than just a café, the new venue will be managed and run by local Community Interest Company, Get Together After Serving (GTAS), and will be staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families Set up by Rochdale residents, Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community in a number of ways, including through wellbeing programmes and local events and get-togethers Customers can expect café favourites like hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts and tea and coffee, alongside generous opening hours and honest prices. The team is also hoping to team up with other local businesses to do specials on Fridays, like curry, pizza and pies. By removing them from the latest version of the Local Plan, we believe we have struck the right balance between supporting economic growth and job creation, providing opportunities for residents, and protecting ou With Gibfield, we simply do not believe the proposals are appropriate and we will make that clear through the consultation. The masterplan requires the council's approval and we cannot support it.”

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. From the streets of New Jersey to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, this is the musical that’s too good to be true. They were just four guys from Jersey, until they sang their very first note. But while their harmonies were perfect on stage, off stage it was a very different story -- a story that has made them an international sensation all over again. The show features all their hits including “Sherry,” “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” “Walk Like A Man,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” “Beggin’,” “December 1963 (Oh What a Night)” and more. It’s been a pleasure to have them with us. We’ve seen their curiosity, eagerness and passion for technology, as well But the success of T Connect has never been something Manchester Digital could deliver alone At its heart, T Connect is about building meaningful connections between technical education and the technology sector. That means giving students opportunities to meet people working in the industry, understand the different careers available to them and, crucially, put their sk Over the past year, businesses and individuals from across our community have helped make that possible in a huge variety of ways - from industry insight sessions and technical masterclasses to mentoring, work experience, office visits and live business projects Our students had the opportunity to learn directly from industry professionals, developing their technical knowledge and getting insight into the tools and approaches used in the workplace Hyperact - Jacob Clark, Director of Engineering, delivered a JavaScript masterclass, helping students strengthen their practical technical knowledge

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned
candidates.evidence_text: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 05 Sep 2026 It was a link forged with blood sweat and tears. It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! candidates.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
